bull_bear.body: Debt-free with INR 700cr surplus; Board recommended final dividend of INR 8/share + interim INR 2.5/share (total INR 10.5/share); all capex funded internally; no M&A or buybacks mentioned
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Raw material supply disruption from Strait of Hormuz; inventory losses if styrene prices fall; non-OEM demand weakness due to high prices and labor/gas shortages; ABS equipment failure impacting utilization; import competition from Taiwan/Korea (though pricing not yet competitive); delayed IOC SM plant affecting Haryana project
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; management acknowledges volatility and supply chain risks but emphasizes operational resilience, domestic demand focus, and capacity utilization improvements; avoids forward guidance on pricing due to fluidity; confident in long-term demand and import substitution potential
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Internal consumption of 14,000 tons of PS/ABS for compounding is excluded from external sales volumes — this masks true production scale; ABS is not currently used in Xmold compounding despite shared parentage; trading revenue (18%) is material and declining, indicating strategic shift toward value-added manufacturing; inventory levels stable at INR 600cr despite supply crunch, suggesting strategic stockpiling
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Strong balance sheet, debt free and meeting all capital expenditure through internal sources.
- SPL remains debt free with investable surplus of INR 874 crores at the end of June 2026.
- Net Debt to Equity (x) was negative across the period shown: -0.55 (FY24), -0.4 (FY25), -0.3 (FY26).
- FY26 returns as stated in the snapshot: RONW 14%; ROCE 21%. The key-highlights chart shows ROE of 17%/18%/14% and ROCE of 24%/24%/21% for FY24/FY25/FY26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Debt-free balance sheet with investible surplus deployed in mutual fund debt schemes, bank fixed deposits and sovereign bonds
- Natural hedge on foreign exchange via exports and import-parity based domestic pricing, supplemented by partial hedging of open FX exposure
- Diversified/proactive international sourcing of Styrene Monomer (including China) allowed the Company to avoid major supply constraints to domestic customers despite Strait of Hormuz disruption
- Long-standing customer relationships across a large number of small and medium sized customers across all geographical areas, sustained despite short-term availability issues
- Entry into automotive-grade compounding (IATF 16949 upgrade at XMold) broadens addressable end-markets beyond appliances
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Feedstock (Styrene Monomer) sourcing concentration in the Middle East — SM, the Company's main raw material, is largely sourced internationally including from Saudi Arabia and Kuwait; the West Asia war and blockage of the Strait of Hormuz stalled these shipments, forcing reliance on China and other alternate sources and pushing up SM prices sharply in March 2026.
- Geopolitical disruption from the West Asia war impacting exports and supply chains — The Company declared force majeure to its export customers after its Middle East SM suppliers declared force majeure; damage to Middle East petrochemical assets is expected to take 4-6 months to normalise post war-end, plus a further 3-4 months for regular shipping availability, delaying export resumption.
- Single-plant operational/equipment risk in the new mABS unit — The newly commissioned mABS plant at Amdoshi had to be shut down in December 2025 due to malfunction of critical production equipment and is currently running at only 65% of installed capacity, showing execution risk in ramping new capacity.
- Import competition and trade-policy risk in Polystyrene — Increased cheaper imports from Thailand, Taiwan, Iran and China (as China becomes self-sufficient in PS and Asian exporters redirect to India) are eroding domestic market share; a zero import-duty dispensation on polymer building blocks (in place up to 30 June 2026) would, if extended, further increase competing imports and discourage new domestic capital investment.
- War-risk insurance gap — The Company has adequately insured its assets against all risks except war risk, leaving asset damage from conflict-related events outside its reinstatement/loss-of-profit insurance cover.
- Foreign exchange volatility — The Company is exposed to dynamic FX rate movements affecting cost and pricing; it only partially hedges open foreign exchange exposure, relying otherwise on a natural hedge from exports and import-parity domestic pricing.
- Cybersecurity and IT-system uptime risk — The business depends on secure, always-available IT systems; despite Tier IV data-centre co-location, SOC/NOC monitoring and periodic third-party security audits, the Company explicitly flags data security and system uptime as essential risk areas requiring continuous mitigation.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Market Leader in Polystyrene and Expanded Polystyrene with market share exceeding 50%, and an internationally reputed supplier of quality Styrenics products.
- India's first and only plant of Extruded Polystyrene Insulation Foam Board (XPS), and India's first truly international scale state-of-art Styrenics complex at Amdoshi.
- SPL was formed as a joint venture between The Supreme Industries Ltd. and the well diversified Rajan Raheja Group.
- ABS is made through 'A FIRST OF ITS KIND Continuous Production Process for ABS in India', claimed to deliver better lot-to-lot consistency, lower base colour, better UV and thermal stability, lower gels, lower VOCs, higher melt strength and less odour.
- Long-term rating maintained at AA-/Stable by CRISIL (outlook revised to Stable); short-term rating remains A1+.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Company acquired M/S Xmold Polymers Pvt Ltd, a Tier II supplier of polymer compounds to producers of components for automobile companies and appliance manufacturers.
- [Geopolitical supply shock] Closure of the Strait of Hormuz due to war in West Asia stopped all liquid and container cargoes from the Gulf and all three Styrene plants in that region - the company's traditional suppliers - shut operations for safety reasons; SPL established alternate supply arrangements to fulfil the total requirements of all its domestic customers.
- [Exports suspended] Exports were suspended due to non-availability of styrene for exports, significant increase in freight rates, reduced shipping capacity availability and increased voyage time.
- [Spread and pricing] Styrene monomer prices in international markets remained elevated with a brief softening near the end of the June quarter before renewed hostilities pushed them up again; the delta between Styrene monomer and Polystyrene improved significantly in the international market during the quarter, while sharp price increases left demand subdued from non-OEM customers.
- [Import duty] Suspension of import duties on commodity polymer, intended to offset the impact of increased import costs, led to increased imports eating away market share of local producers.
business.title: Notable from the deck

The Company operates in the business-to-business (B2B) segment, predominantly serving Original Equipment Manufacturers and a wide spectrum of manufacturing companies across appliance, packaging, automotive and construction-linked end uses, with products reaching customers in 100 countries.

latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth: 8-10% volume growth in FY27 if normalcy returns by June; margin: not specified but expected to improve with volume and stable spreads; order inflow: not quantified; capex/commissioning: INR 250cr total FY27 capex; EPS Phase-II (115ktpa) commissioned April 14, 2026; ABS Phase-II expansion planned for FY28; Haryana project delayed pending IOC SM plant clarity
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Not disclosed; management indicated no new contracts signed due to fluid pricing, but OEMs are buying on spot basis
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: ABS Phase-II expansion (target FY28); EPS export potential to Europe (certified); Xmold expansion into AC OEMs in Sri City; potential de-bottlenecking of PS capacity under evaluation
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Diversify from core Polystyrene/EPS into ABS and mABS (technology from Versalis, Italy) and Speciality Polymer Compounds to access automotive and appliance compounding demand
- Grow the automotive-compounds vertical through subsidiary XMold Polymers (Sri City/Chennai catchment), including SAP integration, grade rationalisation with SPL's range, and upgrading to IATF 16949:2016 including product design capability
- Actively promote EPS in insulation and construction pan-India through customer seminars, industry experts and exhibition participation (Plast India, K-Show, REFCOLD, IGBC, BMTPC)
- Diversify Styrene Monomer sourcing across international markets (including China) to reduce dependence on any single supply corridor after Middle East disruptions
- Fund all capacity expansion from internal accruals, preserving the Company's debt-free balance sheet
- Build a circular economy framework around post-consumer EPS/PS plastic waste via education, NGO/ICPE community partnerships and recycling infrastructure, in line with CPCB Extended Producer Responsibility norms
- Expand greenfield footprint via a new Munak, Haryana site (land acquisition and environmental clearance in progress)
- The Company follows a regular dividend-paying philosophy, confirming an interim dividend already paid during the year and declaring a further final dividend for FY26 at its AGM, indicating shareholder distributions alongside continued reinvestment of profits into capacity-expansion projects.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company commissioned the first phase of its 70,000 MTA brown-field mABS project (technology from Versalis, Italy) at the Amdoshi Complex, Maharashtra in September 2025, along with a 20,000 tpa ABS compounding unit (two lines); the mABS plant was shut down in December 2025 due to a critical equipment malfunction and, per corrective advice from Versalis' Italian technical experts, has restarted at a curtailed 65% of installed capacity, targeted to reach 75-80% during the current year. EPS Phase 2 (30,000 MT capacity) was completed and commissioned in April 2026. A second XPS line of 1,50,000 M3 (wide-width capable) has begun construction, targeted for completion by end of FY27. Separately, the Company is developing a new greenfield site at Munak, Haryana, where land acquisition is nearly complete, the pre-project environmental impact assessment is done, environmental clearance is being pursued, and basic infrastructure/site-grading work is planned for the current year. In April 2025 the Company acquired XMold Polymers Pvt. Ltd. (SIPCOT, Gummidipoondi, near Chennai) to build automotive- and appliance-grade compounding capacity for customers in the Sri City AC-manufacturing cluster; post-acquisition, XMold's operations were integrated onto SAP, its engineering-compound grades were rationalised with SPL's range, and its quality system was upgraded to IATF 16949:2016 (including product design under chapter 8.3).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- GST rationalisation on air conditioners improved affordability and lifted appliance demand in H2 FY26, expected to continue supporting demand
- PLI-scheme-driven investment scale-up in electronics, mobile phones and air conditioner manufacturing is expected to support downstream polymer demand
- RBI projects India GDP growth of 6.9% in FY27, but the ongoing West Asia war and related supply-chain risk (Middle East dependence for energy/petrochemicals) are flagged as headwinds
- Crude oil prices ruling above US$100/barrel are flagged as a risk to India's import bill, rupee parity and inflation, which could soften demand if sustained
- IMD's forecast of a below-normal South-West monsoon is flagged as a risk to rural demand and inflation
- Zero import duty on most polymer building blocks (in place up to 30 June 2026) is easing input costs but simultaneously increasing competing imports and pressuring domestic industry pricing/investment incentive
- Weak PS demand in FY26 attributed to unseasonal rains/milder summer denting cooling-appliance demand, plus rising cheaper imports from Thailand, Taiwan, Iran and China as Chinese PS capacity redirects exports toward India
- New customer AC-manufacturing capacity investments and commissioning of two large-scale export-oriented AC units in South India are expected to support PS demand from H2 of the current year
- PS market expected to grow marginally (~2.5%) in FY27 with OEM demand growing faster (~5%); EPS Indian market expected to grow ~4%; XPS market expected to grow ~20% in FY27 aided by temperature-sensitive packaging demand
- Non-OEM PS demand may see nil-to-negative growth in the current year due to high product prices, tight working capital and reduced gas availability for polymer processing
- Normalisation of Styrene Monomer supply and export resumption is expected roughly 2-6 months after the West Asia war ends, with regular shipping availability taking a further 3-4 months
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Q4FY26 saw strong volume growth and EBITDA margin expansion driven by higher styrene prices and operational efficiency, but full-year profitability was pressured by lower average styrene monomer prices; the key change is the restart of ABS capacity at 65% and commissioning of EPS Phase-II, positioning the company for 8-10% volume growth in FY27 if supply normalizes.

open.item: Sustained crude oil prices above US$100/barrel are flagged as a risk to India's import bill, rupee parity and inflation, with knock-on softening of demand if pressures persist.

Company estimates capital expenditure of about Rs 250 crores in the current year towards ABS Phase II, XPS Phase II, compounding lines and infrastructure augmentation, to be funded from internal accruals.
A second XPS line of 1,50,000 M3 capacity with flexibility to produce wide-width boards is under construction and likely to be completed by end of FY27.

Land acquisition for the Munak site in Haryana is almost complete and pre-project environment impact assessment is done; environment clearance is being sought and basic infrastructure development (site grading) will be taken up during the current year.

Following a December-2025 shutdown from equipment malfunction, the mABS plant is operating at 65% of installed capacity; the Company hopes to achieve around 75-80% of curtailed capacity during the current financial year.
Company expects to grow its Speciality Polymer Compounds (SPC) business by 30% in the current year.

SAN + Glass Filled grades for the AC industry received approval from major Sri City AC makers and commercial supplies began to two customers; the Company plans to bring more such customers into XMold's fold in the current year, backed by a strengthened sales and marketing team.

BIS standards for XPS building insulation could not be finalised during FY26 and are likely to be put in place during the current year, a prerequisite that has constrained the building-insulation segment.
All capital expenditure planned as on date is proposed to be funded from the Company's own funds/internal accruals.

Government reduced import duty to zero on most building blocks and polymers up to June 30, 2026; if this reduction is extended it would increase imports to the detriment of local industry and deter new capital investment in the sector.

open.horizon: 4-6 months post end of war (plant recovery) plus 3-4 months (shipping)
open.item: Damage to Middle East petrochemical assets from the West Asia war is likely to take a minimum of 4 to 6 months to normalise, plus a further 3-4 months for regular availability of ships and shipping space; exports were placed under force majeure.
Company is actively working to promote EPS in insulation and construction applications on a pan-India basis.
All planned capital expenditure is proposed to be funded from the Company's own funds/internal accruals, maintaining its debt-free status.
